notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 8th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 40%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Rasmus Ristolainen is out and has missed the last 4 games. Jamie Drysdale has taken his spot beside Travis Sanheim. That pair has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 55:50 together, up from 23% with Ristolainen.
Nikita Grebenkin is out at least four months (back surgery) and has not played this season. Sean Couturier has taken his spot beside Owen Tippett and Trevor Zegras.
David Jiříček has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 43% of the team’s power-play time in 9 games, up from 2% last season.
Matthew Robertson has not dressed for the last 10 games. Alberts Šmits has taken his spot beside Braden Schneider. That pair has had 45% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 147:08 together.
Sean Durzi is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Braden Schneider has taken his spot beside Marcus Pettersson.
Luke Glendening was added to the roster on Oct 24 and has played beside Taylor Raddysh and Eeli Tolvanen.
James Reimer was added to the roster on Oct 26.
Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
paras: The Flyers (4-9-4) lost 4-2 to Minnesota on Tuesday, while the Rangers (8-7-1) beat St. Louis 3-1 the same night. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Flyers last (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Rangers third (tied for 16th).

The Flyers’ record (.353) is about what their chances are worth. The Rangers have played better than their record (.531) says: their chances are worth about .590, and their finishing has held them back.

The Rangers (32nd) and the Flyers (30th) both get a lot of their shots blocked. The Flyers block more shots than almost anyone (3rd). Philadelphia has scored 2.18 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Rangers get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd lowest). Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, especially the Flyers (2nd lowest), so expect a tight one. Beyond that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Trevor Zegras (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 17 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, with a point in five straight games against the Rangers. Matvei Michkov (10 G / 3 A / 13 P in 17 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for sixth in the NHL. For the Rangers, Adam Fox (2 G / 17 A / 19 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 16 GP) has a team-high nine goals.
Joseph Woll (1-5-2 / .899 SV% in 8 GS) is expected to start for Philadelphia, and Dylan Garand (5-6-1 / .905 SV% in 10 GS) for the Rangers.
At home, Mike Sullivan likes to send Kartye, Miller and Perreault out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Zegras, Dvorak and Konecny.
